statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 23 sits in the watch band and remains below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail is below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields WATCH rather than a block. The narrow flagged window covers the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour running into Friday's quarterly expiration. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ retakes the approach to its session high and NDX prints a marginal new high; Tail firms to 23 and the mapped state stays WATCH
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index is 29,443.12 (+498.06, +1.72%) against Wednesday's 28,945.06 close, having opened at 29,401.54 and just extended the session range to 29,305.90-29,446.51. Price trades roughly 3 points below that newly printed high and about 137 points above the session low. The change from the previous hour is the reassertion: Nasdaq-100 futures are 29,735.75 (+1.64%) within a 29,247.75-29,753.25 range, roughly 18 points beneath the high set before the 13:30 UTC cash open, after sitting about 76 points beneath it an hour earlier. The cash index has therefore confirmed a marginal new high and the continuous futures reference has closed most of its divergence, so the stall of the past three hours is being tested rather than extended sideways. Cross-assets are aligned with that firming. VIX is 15.65 (-11.63%) against a 17.20 prior close, now near the lower end of its 15.38-16.29 session range rather than lifting off the low. The 10-year yield is 4.945% (-6.1 basis points) inside a 4.941%-4.963% range against a 5.006% prior close, close to its session low; the 2-year stood at 4.67% on the September 16 H.15 observation. WTI is near 101.06 dollars (-1.33%) with Brent about 103.58 dollars (-2.13%), easing further as Saudi Arabia routes cargoes through ship-to-ship transfers outside Hormuz and moves to restore roughly half of East-West pipeline capacity within days. Semiconductors lead with SOXX at 519.39 (+3.45%), helped by memory-shortage commentary, and it too now trades just under its 520.42 high. That alignment of index, futures, volatility, rates and semiconductors near session extremes is the reason Tail firms rather than eases. Two counterweights keep it well below the block threshold. The 29,305.90 opening low was bought in a 95-point retracement and has never been retested, and the futures gave back 76 points from the high before recovering, both of which are the two-way behaviour mean reversion requires and the opposite of repeated extension after failed pullbacks. Dispersion also persists: the Dow is up 0.75% and the Russell 2000 1.14% against the Nasdaq Composite's 1.65%, which reads as tech-led rotation rather than a uniform one-way index bid. Thursday's macro cluster resolved cleanly earlier, with initial claims 196,000 against a 208,000 consensus, continuing claims 1,730,000, the Philadelphia Fed index 37.8 against 30.5 expected, housing starts 1.275 million, building permits 1.394 million and pending home sales +0.3% against a -0.6% consensus. The backdrop remains Wednesday's unanimous 12-0 decision to raise the target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase since 2023, with the projections implying one further move this year; markets continue to read that as credibility-positive rather than as fresh directional repricing. Tail therefore firms one point to 23, Stress eases to 51 in the elevated band on continued volatility decay, and Confidence holds at 87 on live cash, futures, volatility, rates, crude and semiconductor evidence plus verified macro actuals and a verified forward calendar. The shared Finviz context was 246 minutes old with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale and partial and was not used as evidence.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours span the FOMC reaction and its unwind. Wednesday's 19:00 UTC hour was the only orange excursion, with Tail 31 and a trend-down mode as the decision and press conference drove a Nasdaq-100 sell-off; that move retraced into the close and Tail fell back to 16-20 overnight. Stress decayed steadily from 79 at the decision to 53 by Thursday afternoon as volatility normalised, the 10-year eased below 5% and crude fell on the Saudi rerouting and restart reporting. The final nine hours carried a trend-up mode with Tail peaking at 26 in the 13:00 UTC hour on opening-auction continuation risk, easing to 22 as that checkpoint resolved with two-way price discovery, and now firming again as the index returns to its session high.
outlookSummary: The current 16:00 UTC hour firms Tail to 23 because the index, futures, volatility, rates and semiconductors are simultaneously near session extremes, while the bought opening low and the futures' own 76-point give-back keep two-way structure intact. Conditional Tail then eases to 21 through the quiet US mid-afternoon on the assumption that rotation replaces directional efficiency, lifts back to 23 for the flagged 19:00 UTC power hour into Friday's quarterly expiration, and carries an event/whipsaw mode across the 20:00 UTC cash close for closing-imbalance risk; none of that structure has been observed. Overnight slots settle at 16-17 on the absence of scheduled catalysts, with Stress bottoming at 41 in the moderate band. Conditional Tail then firms back through Friday's European open and expiration fixing windows and peaks at 23 for the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours, where the 13:15 UTC Industrial Production release stacks against the quarterly expiration cash open. Confidence declines from 87 to 61 with forecast distance because evidence quality degrades, not because the risk picture deteriorates.
